architecture: YOLOv8 (C2f backbone, Detect head), 25.86M parameters, Ultralytics 8.4.7, trained at 1024 px

operating_point.description: Inference settings used by AwaazIQ. The weights are unchanged.

checkpoint_own_validation.note: Metrics stored inside the checkpoint by its training run, on its own validation split. Optimistic: same source as the training data.

image_level.name: Held-out real photos (Wikimedia, 25 countries + Indian roads)
image_level.note: Never used to choose any setting. 37 clear potholes, 46 pothole-free roads (44 in Kerala, Karnataka, Gujarat, Tamil Nadu), 5 hard negatives (river potholes, a diagram, a sign).

image_level.name: Tuning set (Wikimedia: India, USA, Germany potholes; asphalt and Maharashtra roads)
image_level.note: Used to choose the operating point, so its operating-point numbers are optimistic.

image_level.name: taroii/pothole-detection test split (224 px thumbnails)
image_level.note: Tiny 224x224 images, far below the 1024 px the model expects, so recall is low.

box_level.dataset: Ryukijano/Pothole-detection-Yolov8 (Roboflow 'Potholes Detection' v1) test split: 100 images, 269 pothole boxes
box_level.note: Its labels also box patched repairs and tiny distant potholes, which this model does not call potholes, so box metrics understate it.

structural_damage.note: The crack class was trained on road surfaces; it is a weak proxy for bridge or building damage.

C7_moire.note: Recaptures simulated physically (RGB sub-pixel display, lens blur, rotated camera sampling). Not yet measured on real phone photos of screens.

C7_burst.note: Identical frames (still image through a virtual camera) are flagged; frames with sensor noise are not. Unit-tested on synthetic frames.

C4_error_level.note: Cannot tell genuine from spliced photos, so the score is advisory only and never lowers trust. Editing-software metadata is the C4 signal that counts.

C3_duplicates.note: Perceptual hash matches resized and recompressed copies; unrelated scenes do not match (unit-tested).

limits: On held-out real photos it catches about 86% of potholes, and about 1 in 4 alerts is a false alarm, mostly dirt roads and busy junctions.
Water-filled potholes, holes full of debris and very small or distant potholes are missed more often.
Low-resolution photos (e.g. 224 px) lose most detections.
The crack class is trained on roads; it rarely fires on bridge or building damage (1 of 8 photos), so C6 leans on the complaint's wording.
Screen-replay detection was calibrated on simulated recaptures; edit detection (ELA) is advisory only.
Every result is a signal for an officer, never a verdict: photos only raise or lower confidence.
